claim: Intensive glycemic control reduces cardiovascular events in type 2 diabetes
gold_rationale: The three purpose-built cardiovascular-outcome RCTs of intensive glycemic control in high-CV-risk T2D converge against the claim. ACCORD (NEJM 2008, PMID 18539917) was STOPPED EARLY because intensive therapy INCREASED all-cause mortality (HR 1.22, 95% CI 1.01-1.46) and did not significantly reduce the primary MACE composite (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.78-1.04, P=0.16); it did reduce nonfatal MI (HR 0.76) but at the cost of excess death. ADVANCE (PMID 18539916) showed no effect on major macrovascular events (HR 0.94, P=0.32), CV death (HR 0.88, P=0.12), or all-cause death (HR 0.93, P=0.28) — its positive combined primary endpoint was driven by a reduction in microvascular nephropathy, a different endpoint. VADT (PMID 19092145) showed no effect on major CV events (HR 0.88, P=0.14) or death (HR 1.07). The prospectively planned CONTROL-group meta-analysis (Turnbull, Diabetologia 2009, PMID 19655124; 27,049 patients, 2,370 events) found only a modest 9% reduction in major CV events (HR 0.91, 0.84-0.99) driven by a 15% MI reduction (HR 0.85), with NO mortality benefit (all-cause HR 1.04; CV death HR 1.10) and a 2.5-fold excess of severe hypoglycemia (HR 2.48); benefit was absent in those with pre-existing macrovascular disease. UKPDS 33 (PMID 9742976) in newly diagnosed patients showed no significant macrovascular benefit during the trial. The only clear mortality benefit — UKPDS 34 metformin (PMID 9742977, 36% all-cause mortality reduction) — is a metformin-specific, newly-diagnosed-population, legacy-effect finding, not evidence that lowering glycemia per se reduces CV events in the high-risk population of the claim. Consensus (ADA Standards of Care 2023 and ACP guidance): guidelines moved to individualized HbA1c targets and caution against tight control in high-CV-risk/long-duration patients; of the three trials achieving HbA1c <7%, none reduced all-cause or CV death. The claim as stated is Not Supported.
outcome: MACE (nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke, CV death) and all-cause/CV mortality
population: Type 2 diabetes at high cardiovascular risk (established CVD or multiple risk factors; typically longer-duration disease)
provenance: PubMed-verified landmark RCTs and a prospectively planned group-level meta-analysis; all six PMIDs, DOIs, abstracts, Ns, and effect sizes independently re-confirmed via get_article_metadata. Gold consensus corroborated against ADA Standards of Care 2023 (dc23-s006) and ACP guidance (M17-0939). No retractions found.
notes: Surrogate/endpoint-mismatch detection is decisive for ADVANCE: its positive primary composite is driven by microvascular nephropathy, NOT the claimed MACE/mortality outcome (macrovascular and mortality components null) — outcome_match=false. UKPDS 33/34 populations are NEWLY DIAGNOSED, not the high-CV-risk population of the claim — population_match=false; UKPDS 34's benefit is metformin-specific rather than a glycemia-lowering effect. No dramatic_effect anywhere: chronic disease with an actively CONTRADICTING RCT (ACCORD showing harm), the opposite of an all-or-none fatal-disease rescue. The strongest pro-claim datum (Turnbull meta-analysis) still shows no mortality benefit. Re-verification found every PMID, N, HR, and design correct; ACCORD's nonfatal-MI component was in fact reduced (HR 0.76), which does not change the Not Supported verdict since MACE was null and mortality increased.

rows.citation: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD) Study Group. Effects of intensive glucose lowering in type 2 diabetes. N Engl J Med. 2008;358(24):2545-59. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa0802743
rows.integrity_note: Landmark NIH-funded RCT (NCT00000620); intensive arm stopped early for excess mortality. No retraction; standard RCT article type confirmed on PubMed.
rows.finding: N=10,251 high-CV-risk T2D (35% prior CV event). Intensive therapy (target HbA1c <6%; achieved 6.4% vs 7.5%) did NOT significantly reduce the primary MACE composite (352 vs 371 events; HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.78-1.04, P=0.16) and INCREASED all-cause mortality (257 vs 203 deaths; HR 1.22, 95% CI 1.01-1.46, P=0.04). Intensive regimen halted at mean 3.5y. Nonfatal MI was reduced (HR 0.76, 0.62-0.92) but offset by excess death. Directly contradicts the claim on the mortality/MACE limb.

rows.citation: ADVANCE Collaborative Group. Intensive blood glucose control and vascular outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes. N Engl J Med. 2008;358(24):2560-72. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa0802987
rows.integrity_note: Large independent RCT (NCT00145925); no retraction. Positive PRIMARY composite is microvascular-driven, not MACE.
rows.finding: N=11,140 T2D (median 5y follow-up; achieved HbA1c 6.5% vs 7.3%). NO significant effect on major MACROVASCULAR events (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.84-1.06, P=0.32), CV death (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.74-1.04, P=0.12), or all-cause death (HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.83-1.06, P=0.28). The positive combined primary endpoint (HR 0.90) was driven by a 21% reduction in nephropathy (microvascular) — a SURROGATE/endpoint mismatch to the claimed CV-event outcome. Neutral on MACE/mortality.

rows.citation: Duckworth W, et al. (VADT). Glucose control and vascular complications in veterans with type 2 diabetes. N Engl J Med. 2009;360(2):129-39. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa0808431
rows.integrity_note: VA-funded RCT (NCT00032487) in long-standing T2D; no retraction. PubMed indexes entry 2008-12-17; journal issue 2009;360(2). Year 2009 retained per citation.
rows.finding: N=1,791 veterans with poorly-controlled long-standing T2D (mean 11.5y since dx; 40% prior CV event). Intensive control (median HbA1c 6.9% vs 8.4%) had NO significant effect on major CV events (235 vs 264; HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.74-1.05, P=0.14) and no effect on all-cause death (HR 1.07, 95% CI 0.81-1.42, P=0.62). Excess adverse events, predominantly hypoglycemia (24.1% vs 17.6%). Neutral — does not support the claim.

rows.citation: Turnbull FM, et al. (Control Group). Intensive glucose control and macrovascular outcomes in type 2 diabetes. Diabetologia. 2009;52(11):2288-98. DOI:10.1007/s00125-009-1470-0
rows.integrity_note: Prospectively planned group-level meta-analysis pooling ACCORD/ADVANCE/VADT/UKPDS with pre-specified outcomes; indexed Meta-Analysis, no retraction.
rows.finding: Pooled N=27,049; 2,370 major vascular events over 4.4y. Intensive control gave a MODEST 9% reduction in major CV events (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.84-0.99), driven by a 15% MI reduction (HR 0.85, 0.76-0.94). Crucially NO mortality benefit: all-cause HR 1.04 (0.90-1.20), CV death HR 1.10 (0.84-1.42); severe hypoglycemia HR 2.48 (1.91-3.21). Benefit absent in those with pre-existing macrovascular disease (HR 1.00 vs 0.84; interaction P=0.04). Weak MI signal but null on the mortality limb of the claim.

rows.citation: UK Prospective Diabetes Study (UKPDS) Group. Intensive blood-glucose control with sulphonylureas or insulin compared with conventional treatment (UKPDS 33). Lancet. 1998;352(9131):837-53.
rows.integrity_note: Foundational long-term RCT; no retraction. Population is NEWLY DIAGNOSED (median age 54), not high-CV-risk.
rows.finding: N=3,867 NEWLY diagnosed T2D (median age 54, low baseline CV risk). Intensive control cut microvascular endpoints 25% (P=0.0099) but showed NO significant macrovascular benefit: any-diabetes-related endpoint 12% lower (P=0.029, largely microvascular) and all-cause mortality only 6% lower (95% CI -10 to 20, P=0.44); MI reduction ~16% did not reach significance (P~0.052). Population mismatch to the high-risk claim; neutral on macrovascular events during the trial.

rows.citation: UK Prospective Diabetes Study (UKPDS) Group. Effect of intensive blood-glucose control with metformin (UKPDS 34). Lancet. 1998;352(9131):854-65.
rows.integrity_note: RCT sub-study; no retraction. Benefit is metformin-specific and in newly-diagnosed overweight patients — not a general glycemia-lowering effect in high-risk T2D.
rows.finding: N=753 overweight NEWLY diagnosed T2D (342 metformin vs 411 diet; median 10.7y). Metformin arm reduced all-cause mortality 36% (95% CI 9-55, P=0.011), diabetes-related death 42% (P=0.017), and any diabetes-related endpoint 32% (P=0.002) vs diet. A genuine mortality benefit — but drug-specific (metformin outperformed the SU/insulin arms) and in a low-risk newly-diagnosed population. Supports metformin, not the broad high-risk claim.

baseline.text: No. Intensive glycemic control does not reliably reduce cardiovascular events in type 2 diabetes, and in high-risk patients it can be harmful. The pivotal ACCORD trial was stopped early because targeting near-normal HbA1c INCREASED all-cause mortality (HR 1.22) without reducing the primary MACE composite. ADVANCE and VADT both found no significant reduction in macrovascular events or mortality. Meta-analyses show at most a modest reduction in nonfatal MI but no reduction in cardiovascular or all-cause death, offset by a roughly 2-3x increase in severe hypoglycemia. The main mortality benefit historically cited (UKPDS metformin arm) is drug-specific and in newly diagnosed patients, not evidence that intensive glucose lowering itself reduces CV events in high-risk T2D. Consequently guidelines shifted to individualized HbA1c targets rather than uniformly tight control. The claim is not supported.
